However, we should also consider what is often called the innovator’s dilemma, a term coined by Harvard professor Clayton Christensen. 78 If Google brought forward a chatbot that could effectively replace Search, it faced a giant innovator’s dilemma. Google’s massive ad revenue stream (more than $200 billion annually from Search) relies on a specific user behavior: Searching >> Scrolling >> Clicking. 79 In the search engine model, you ask a question, Google gives you a list of links (with ads at the top), and the company gets paid when you click those ads. But in a chatbot model, you ask a question, and the AI gives you the answer. If the AI gives you the answer directly, you have no reason to scroll and click on a link. In the industry, this is called a zero-click search. For Google, a perfect AI chatbot is a product that potentially destroys its own ad inventory. As a venture-backed entrepreneur, one of the things you learn early on is that you actually can innovate in areas where large incumbent companies should be able to use their resources to innovate much faster and where they already have distribution scale, arguably making it impossible for you to achieve scale and build your business. You see, when innovating in a particular way would threaten an incumbent’s core revenue stream, a start-up can step in, raise tens of millions of dollars, build the product, and bring it to market. The innovator’s dilemma is well understood, and Silicon Valley takes advantage of it all the time. So, while I cannot know how they were thinking about this, it is safe to say that the people at Google had some incentive to not create a consumer-facing option. Though they may have been planning to at some point. And the AI was complex enough that only a relatively small number of people deeply understood it, and the substantial model training cost made it difficult for a typically funded start-up to take it on. And so, AI was being advanced as a corporate tool, and not something to put in your hands as an individual. AI was something that would happen to you , not be used by you . This is not a judgment of Google. We would not be where we are with this magnificent AI without Google. And Gemini, the company’s now available chatbot, is arguably the best in the market. Which is not a big surprise when you understand the history. Back to this disagreement between Elon Musk and Larry Page that I believe changed the trajectory of humankind. 80 Elon has reported this conversation in multiple venues and podcasts. According to his telling, Elon was often talking with Larry Page about the safety risks of artificial intelligence and the need to set up guardrails and the risk that it might run away and have a catastrophic impact on humans. At some point in that argument, Elon has claimed that Larry famously asked him if he was a “speciesist.” 81 To which Elon claims to have answered, “Yes, I am very much a speciesist, and you should be too. We have to protect this dim light of consciousness in the universe.” According to Elon, when he could not get Larry to adjust his position, he decided that he would start OpenAI, a nonprofit consumer-facing AI chatbot that later became ChatGPT, which you can get now. 82 I think that backstory is important. But for that heated disagreement, the value of AI may have been held in the hands of a few large companies for some time into the future. But with the advent of ChatGPT and Claude and now Google’s amazing Gemini, basically anyone can plug into AI and enrich their minds and their lives. For that, I am very thankful. And I think it will prove to have changed the trajectory of humankind with artificial intelligence. So now that it is in our hands, on our phones and computers, how will we plug in? An Old Story with Modern Implications When I was a junior in high school in 1981, I called the offices of several CEOs of large companies with local headquarters in Dallas, where I lived. I would usually get their admin. Here was my pitch: “I want to break the poverty cycle and become an entrepreneur, and I am trying to figure out what to study in college, and I would really appreciate if I could come by and spend fifteen minutes with your CEO to ask his thoughts and share a cup of coffee.” To my great surprise, each call I made got me a meeting. I would later see a video of Steve Jobs telling a similar story and challenging young people to simply reach out and ask, saying how surprised they would be at the response. I certainly can vouch for that. Anyway, one of those CEOs ran a large commercial real estate development company. As we sat for coffee, we became fast friends (or, perhaps more accurately, he became a fast mentor to me), and the next year, when I graduated from high school, he offered me a part-time job in his company while I went to college. The company had hundreds of millions of dollars in real estate development projects. I was trained by his finance team on how to update these giant spreadsheets by hand (yes, they were on paper !). So, when an updated number came in from the field, my job was to carefully change that number in the paper spreadsheet and then manually calculate every downstream number and erase and update until the entire spreadsheet was updated.
